rulers.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'In June 1956, Nasser assumed the presidency'; the page does not name the head of state between 1954 and June 1956 (the list has a gap).

keyframe_review.note: 1,011,422 km2 against the infobox's 1,010,408 km2 (ratio 1.00). The shape includes the Sinai, the Egyptian-administered Gaza Strip (2 cells, 'After the 1948 Arab-Israeli War, Egypt occupied the Gaza Strip') and a strip of about 5,000 km2 along the 22nd parallel that reaches into Sudan (cell-edge noise, or the Halaib claim; the pages opened say nothing). Sudan became independent on 1 January 1956 ('granting Sudan full independence').

correction.text: the 1953 shape unchanged: the Sinai and Gaza stay Egyptian, occupied by Israel (hatched) from November 1956 to March 1957

keyframe_review.note: 948,759 km2: the shape gives the Sinai (about 47,000 km2) and Gaza to Israel for 1956 and 1957 (Cliopatria's Israel shape 1956-1957 holds them). The occupation lasted 'until March 1957' only, and was not annexation; the ledger carries it as occupation_start/end, so the Egyptian shape keeps the Sinai. For the Port Said landing see the ledger.

region.text: Egypt, with the Sinai and the Egyptian-administered Gaza Strip

ledger.note: 18 June 1953: Egypt becomes a republic. 'On 18 June 1953, the Republic of Egypt was officially declared,' with Muhammad Naguib as first president; the revolution was 22-23 July 1952. Same land as the kingdom (kingdom-of-egypt ends the same day).

region.text: the Suez Canal Zone (same outline as the kingdom-of-egypt dossier)

ledger.note: June 1953: British troops still hold the Suez Canal Zone. The occupation began in 1922 (kingdom-of-egypt dossier); the Egypt page only shows it ending: 'In October 1954, Egypt and the United Kingdom agreed to end the' occupation and 'British forces completed their withdrawal from the Suez Canal Zone on 13 June 1956'. The start year here is inherited, the page is silent on 1953.

region.text: the Suez Canal Zone (same outline as the kingdom-of-egypt dossier)

ledger.note: 13 June 1956: the last British troops leave the Canal Zone. 'British forces completed their withdrawal from the Suez Canal Zone on 13 June 1956' under the October 1954 agreement; Nasser became president in June 1956.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

ledger.note: 29 October 1956: Israel invades the Sinai. 'Israel invaded on 29 October, with the primary objective of re-opening the Straits of Tiran'; Egypt had nationalised the canal on 26 July 1956. 'On 2 November, Bar-Lev's forces took al-Arish'; 'By noon of 3 November, the Israelis had control of almost the entire Gaza Strip'.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

ledger.note: November 1956: the fighting stops. The Egyptian commander surrendered Sharm el-Sheikh on 5 November; the ceasefire took effect on 6-7 November ('Ben-Gurion told the Knesset that the armistice lines were no longer valid'). The page gives no single date for the end of the Israeli-Egyptian fighting.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

ledger.note: November 1956: Israel holds the Sinai and Gaza. 'Israel's four-month-long occupation'; infobox 'Israeli occupation of the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip until March 1957'. Egypt keeps the title: Cliopatria's Republic of Egypt 1956-1957 shape drops the Sinai, which the keyframe review corrects.

region.text: the Port Said area at the northern end of the canal, where British paratroopers landed at El Gamil and Royal Marines stormed the beaches

ledger.note: 5-6 November 1956: British paratroops and Royal Marines land at Port Said. 'In the early morning of 5 November, an advance element of the' paratroopers dropped on El Gamil Airfield; 'At first light on 6 November, Royal Marines of No. 42 and 40 Commando stormed the beaches'; British forces were at al-Cap when the ceasefire came into effect. France took part (Port Fuad, not named on the page excerpt).

region.text: the Port Said area at the northern end of the canal, where British paratroopers landed at El Gamil and Royal Marines stormed the beaches

ledger.note: 1956: the Anglo-French force leaves. 'Britain and France agreed to withdraw from Egypt within a week; Israel did not.' The page gives no completion date; the month is bridged from that sentence (an agreement of 6-7 November to leave within a week), and the actual departure may have been later.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

ledger.note: March 1957: Israel leaves the Sinai and Gaza. Infobox: 'Israeli occupation of the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip until March 1957'; the Canal reopened in March 1957 ('closed from October 1956 to March 1957').

1958: Egypt unites with Syria. 'In 1958, Egypt formed a political union with Syria, creating the United Arab Republic.' The united-arab-republic dossier dates it February 1958 (not read here). Syria seceded in 1961. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: month from the United Arab Republic page: 'established on 1 February 1958'.]

1958: the Republic of Egypt becomes the Egyptian region of the United Arab Republic. Egypt took the name Arab Republic of Egypt again in 1971 ('renamed the country the Arab Republic of Egypt in 1971'); Cliopatria dates the Republic of Egypt 1953-1957. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: month from the United Arab Republic page: 'established on 1 February 1958'.]

wars.name: Suez Crisis

zones.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip
the Port Said area at the northern end of the canal, where British paratroopers landed at El Gamil and Royal Marines stormed the beaches

wars.outcome: Israel overran the Sinai and Gaza and held them until March 1957; Britain and France landed at Port Said on 5-6 November 1956 and agreed to withdraw within a week; the Canal was closed from October 1956 to March 1957. 'The conflict ended following diplomatic pressure from the United States and the Soviet Union.'
wars.note: The Egypt page gives the nationalisation as the trigger only indirectly; the Suez page has 'On 26 July 1956, in a speech in Alexandria, Nasser announced the nationalisation of the canal.'

certainty.note: The pages opened survey no frontier: the desert borders with Libya and Sudan are approximate; the line with Israel is the 1949 armistice line (see the state-of-israel dossier), sharp; the Canal Zone and the Gaza Strip were held or administered by others at times.

notes: Written by me-10-j from two pages (the page budget). SHARED WIKIDATA Q79 with arab-republic-of-egypt (Cliopatria 1973-2024): treated as DIFFERENT dossiers. Between them stands the United Arab Republic (1958-1971, its own dossier from another part, whose predecessor is this one and whose successor is arab-republic-of-egypt) and the two Cliopatria rows are separated by 1958-1972 where Egypt is the UAR's region; the colour agent may still want to give the three the same colour (rule 2: same land, a state that changed its name), in which case the UAR and Arab Republic dossiers carry the continuity. END DATE: the Egypt page gives only 'In 1958'; Cliopatria ends the row in 1957 and starts the UAR in 1958. The united-arab-republic dossier has February 1958 (not read here). GAZA: the Egyptian-administered Gaza Strip is inside the Cliopatria shape; its status (the All-Palestine Protectorate of 1948 to June 1959 and the later 'occupation' recorded in the united-arab-republic dossier) is in the kingdom-of-egypt, all-palestine-government and united-arab-republic dossiers; the Israeli occupation of Gaza in 1956-1957 is here. SUDAN: independence on 1 January 1956 ends the condominium; Egypt owned no Sudanese land on these pages. NOT READ: the 1952 Revolution page, the 1954 evacuation agreement, the Canal's nationalisation beyond the Suez page, the Anglo-French withdrawal date, French counterpart (France as the Fourth Republic has no dossier named here; the Port Said events carry kingdom-of-great-britain only).
